I took over the baseapp a few days ago yeah (as well as trading products in Coinbase - the Coinbase app, Advanced trading, etc). I don’t run Base chain.

I think that typically CB has been a little bit in an ivory tower and a little bit distant from users, particularly crypto natives. I don’t think I will be able to fix that in a week, or maybe even a month. I can try and capture the voice of ppl onchain more and try and align ppl building things more closely w users. Obviously CB/Base has burned a lot of user goodwill w those users thru some unforced errors, including today. 

Obviously I could simply not do any of these things and have a nice life instead. Lots of ppl, including og base supporters/trenchers, rly hate base rn - throwing myself into the middle of a hatred pile-on is clearly not the most optimal life choice. I am aware I am setting myself up to be blamed by association. So, I wouldn’t be doing this if I thought it were impossible. 

I’m going to try and ship stuff that ppl like to use. Maybe ppl will hate what I do w the baseapp too, we will see how it goes.

每次我去一个不同国家的地区基本都会带一些当地特色的酒，这次日本本来是想带日本酒的，所以主要看的都是日本酒，但日本酒我就不是很懂了，基本都是问的 ChatGPT，那些值得买。

ChatGPT 给我的排序在不限制预算的情况下（日元）：

第一名：IWA 5（约 ¥20,000）

第二名：穗田秋田（穂田秋田）纯米大吟酿（约 ¥40,000）

第三名：久保田 万寿（约 ¥23,900）

第四名：八海山 三年熟成（约 ¥20,000）

第五名：獭祭（高端版）

第六名：作（ZAKU）

本来我是准备买 IWA 5 或者 穂田秋田 了，然后 ChatGPT 建议我先不要着急下手，去逛逛威士忌区，说如果今天能碰到 山崎18年、白州18年、响21年，它们的稀缺性、升值空间和国际认可度，整体都高于现在看到的大多数清酒。

结果我就去看威士忌了，然后就没有日本酒的事情了，ChatGPT 的排名如下：

响21年 ≈ 山崎18年 > 白州18年 > IWA 5 > 久保田万寿 > 八海山三年熟成。

������没想到昨天大家最感兴趣的竟然是这一条，而且很多小伙伴都惊呼值了，看来我朋友圈的小伙伴喜欢酒的还真不少啊，这瓶 响 21（Hibiki 21 Years Old）确实比较难买，官方配额极少。

即便是在日本的二手市场通常在 15 万到20 多万日元，当然不同版本和年份还会更高。所以机场能以 10 万日元买到属于很不错的价格了，而且我尝试问买两三瓶的时候竟然和我说可以买。

但新加坡只能带入境 1L 的烈酒，多了就要交税了，而且新加坡酒水的税并不便宜，我考虑了很久还是放弃了。另外免税店的 山崎18年 和 白州18年 只要样品了，着两瓶酒也是可遇不可求的。

下边的这个照片是三组日本机场免税店限定版，平时在日本酒铺基本买不到的，性价比非常高。

一般市场的排名分别是：

1. 山崎 Smoky Batch（右边）

2. 白州 Japanese Forest（中间）

3. 响 Master's Select（左边）

其中 Master's Select 是真正机场限定，但收藏市场来说 山崎 > 白州 > 响

我是真没想到机场的免税店竟然就有售，早知道就应该让小伙伴帮我多带几瓶了。这瓶不论是自己收藏还是送礼都是非常好的。

The issue is that all of that data still winds up in Bitcoin. Op return isn’t even the cheapest place to put it, it’s just historically the least harmful place to put it (that’s why it exists).

All of this fork discussion is basically a debate about which bucket to put spam into, since there isn’t a proposal on the table to materially reduce spam or materially increase the cost of the cheapest method to spam.

That’s why I didn’t bother to talk about it over the past year. And I’d see tweets regularly tagging me asking why I’m not talking about it, people claiming it’s the biggest thing and I’m not talking about it (it’s not the biggest thing. I had little reason to talk about a fork with low consensus that doesn’t materially reduce spam.) I have people emailing asking me if Bitcoin is going to die if a fork that just mildly re-arranges where spam goes doesn’t pass (because they somehow think it stops spam, and its leading proponents have called spam an emergency in need of a rapid fix).

Then I’m asked about it on a podcast. So I explained that it’s not an emergency, the fork doesn’t materially stop spam, it comes with some trade-offs, bitcoin is fine, it’s always worth exploring ways to optimize bitcoin for the future, etc.

Then I get dozens of replies from fork proponents asking if I’m compromised, why do I like spam, why don’t I want to stop spam, etc. Most of them (not all) have playground-grade ad hominems attached as well. It’s mostly not their fault though; they’ve been whipped into a frenzy by people saying if they don’t pass this fork then bitcoin dies.

I support people trying to fork if they want to. Bitcoin needs market tests once in a while. But if people ask me my opinion about this fork’s technical merits, the marketing around it, or its probability of becoming consensus, I’ll give my opinion.

好问题，首先，开源≠开放权重。

Kimi 开放的是权重，这等于免去了最贵的第一次预训练，但是也没到开盒即用的水平，就好比你开放法拉利的设计图纸，距离生产出法拉利还有一段距离。

其次，这个是培养用户习惯的低成本方式。

你看那些海外的开发者在各种中转站、API 买 Kimi 和 GLM 的 Token 你就知道了，不需要太多的广告投入，就能换来核心社区的核心用户，这是成本的考虑。

你看 Gemini 和 ChatGPT 在美国投了多少广告才换来那些开发者使用？

第三，我觉得每个真的下载权重，去部署本地 AI 的人都知道，本地确实非常难用。

有那个折腾的功夫，真的不如直接买正版 API。

个人如此、企业如此，其他国家亦如此。反正国产 AI 价格一个比一个便宜，所以运维、推理折腾成本<直接买现成 Kimi K3/GLM 5.2 Token 成本。

最后，道义上，也许 Kimi 确实蒸馏了一部分友商的 AI，这本来是站在道德低点的。

结果，它反手一个开源（权重），一下子正义多了������，反而有点罗宾汉的感觉，所以开放权重，也有道义上的考虑吧。

I have no firm view on what size op return should be. And my level of concern for its size is low because all that content can still go into bitcoin anyway.\n\nPeople that are hardcore about this distinction tend to fall into one of two camps in my observation: 1) they care more about intention than outcomes (ie it still winds up in there, but only “unofficially”) or 2) they care a lot about making a government compliant coin (with the issue being that bitcoin is global and national laws frequently change).
